analysis_details:
- I inspected the relevant protection-service entrypoints in [ProtectionService.java](/opt/keycloak-source/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/protection/ProtectionService.java#L57) and confirmed that the authz management surface is split by scope and purpose. `resource_set` and `permission/ticket` are on a protected path, and `uma-policy` is routed to `UserManagedPermissionService`.
- In [UserManagedPermissionService.java](/opt/keycloak-source/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/protection/policy/UserManagedPermissionService.java#L74) and [UserManagedPermissionService.java](/opt/keycloak-source/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/protection/policy/UserManagedPermissionService.java#L149), the service explicitly enforces resource ownership, owner-managed access, and resource-scope validity before creating or updating UMA policies. The update path also rejects any attempt to change the associated resource set.
- I validated this against the live lab with real user bearer tokens. `marta` could create a normal UMA policy on her own resource, but the same `POST` with `resources:["27776d0b-855f-40df-b1ff-dbc4bf20dd11"]` in the payload was rejected with `400 invalid_request` and the message `Only resource owner can access policies for resource [27776d0b-855f-40df-b1ff-dbc4bf20dd11]`.
- `kolo` could not use the protection-management endpoints at all: `GET /realms/anypoc/authz/protection/resource_set` returned `403 Forbidden` for the victim user, while `marta`’s token succeeded. That is consistent with intended access control, not a cross-user write issue.
- Net: I did not find a normal HTTP/API flow where one ordinary user can cause authorization state on another user’s protected resource to change. The report appears to be a false positive or an overbroad speculation.
